title: I’m building StoneEra solo with AI-assisted assets — now I’m preparing the first playable demo
author: Arrock12
selftext:
I’ve been developing StoneEra solo, and I’m now getting the first public demo ready for Steam.



This video is around 10 minutes of actual gameplay compressed into 2 minutes.



AI has become part of my workflow mainly on the content side. For some assets, I start with an idea, generate visual references from multiple angles, and then use those references while building and adjusting the actual models in Blender.



I’ve also been experimenting with AI for music, sound ideas, concept exploration, and speeding up some of the repetitive parts of development.



The actual game systems — procedural world generation, NPC jobs, building, crafting, farming, hunting, dynamic water and water management — are systems I’ve been developing and integrating into the game itself.



I’m currently testing version 0.9.10 and planning to submit the first demo to Steam for review within the next few days.



For other solo developers using AI: where has it actually saved you the most time without taking control of the creative process?

replies.body: That’s very interesting. Why didn’t you finish it?

comments.author: lukebuckley1
comments.body:
Nice, how did you generate the Art Assets? I've been wanting to try this, as I think its an AI friendly style, but also looks visually nice to players. Wouldn't mind knowing how you tackled the animation also.

I'm afraid I can't answer your question, as I haven't really utilised it...Yet. I'm looking to speed up my coding process using Qwen 3.8 27B locally (I tried codex but would quickly run out of tokens on a $20 subscription). I need to strike a balance between having it do everything and me understanding the code so I could edit it without the use of AI

replies.author: Arrock12
replies.body:
For the art assets, I started by generating a lot of reference images and combining different ideas until I got something close to what I wanted. Then I used AI to help me recreate those concepts as 3D models in Blender.  
It definitely wasn’t a one-click process though. I had to make a lot of corrections and adjustments in Blender before getting the final models I was happy with.  
I handled the animations in Blender as well, with AI helping along the way.  
For coding, I’m currently using Codex Pro 20x. It’s a huge improvement over the $20 plan for my workflow, but even with 20x there are times when I manage to burn through the limits 😅  
And yeah, I agree about the shadows. They’re there, but currently way too subtle. That’s something I need to improve.

replies.author: thecrustycrap
replies.body: Is Codex Pro 20x worth the subscription? Currently using Claude Pro

replies.author: Arrock12
replies.body:
For me, yes. I use Codex a lot, and Pro 20x has been worth it, especially when working on larger parts of the project where it needs a lot of context.  
That said, I still manage to hit the limits sometimes .So it really depends on how heavily you use it. If Claude Pro is already covering your workload, I wouldn’t switch just for the sake of switching.
